NEW YORK (CNN) -- Topps Meat Co. on Saturday expanded a recall of ground beef from about 300,000  pounds to 21.7 million pounds, one of the largest meat recalls in U.S. history. The recalled products are all ground beef patties with various brand names. In a statement, the Elizabeth, New Jersey, company said the hamburger patties may be contaminated with E. coli O157:H7, a bacterium that can cause severe diarrhea and cramps, as well as other complications. A statement from the U.S. Department of Agriculture said 25 illnesses are under investigation in Connecticut, Florida, Indiana, Maine, New Jersey, New York, Ohio and Pennsylvania. The ground beef products being recalled have a "sell by date" or a "best if used by date" between September 25, 2007, and September 25, 2008, Topps' statement said.  Watch the latest on the beef recall » . The packages also have the marking "Est. 9748" inside the USDA mark of inspection. Tuesday, the company announced a recall of about 331,000 pounds of hamburger meat, according to the USDA. "Because the health and safety of our consumers is our top priority, we are taking these expansive measures," said Vice President of Operations Geoffrey Livermore in the statement. "Topps is continuing to work with the USDA, state departments of health, retailers and distributors to ensure the safety of our consumers. Additionally, we have augmented our internal quality control procedures with microbiologists and food safety experts. We sincerely regret any inconvenience and concerns this may cause our consumers," Livermore said. This is the company's first recall in its 65 years of business, the statement said. Consumers who find the products at home are asked to cut off the UPC code and return it to Topps for a full refund, then dispose of the product immediately, Topps spokeswoman Michelle Williams said. The company said to avoid E. coli, consumers should wash hands thoroughly after handling the beef. Topps set up a toll-free recall help line at (888) 734-0451. Williams said because the products may have been produced up to a year ago, many of them have already been safely consumed. Production in the ground beef area of the company's plant in Elizabeth has been shut down until all the investigations are complete, Williams said in a phone interview. "We're working with the USDA and the CDC [Centers for Disease Control and Prevention] and conducting our own investigation," she added. The products, all ground beef patties and hamburgers with various brand names, were distributed mainly in the northeastern United States, but went to retailers in many other areas of the country as well, Williams said. While the sheer size of the recall is large, two other companies have been involved in larger recalls. In 2002, Pilgrim's Pride recalled more than 27 million pounds of poultry, and Hudson Foods recalled 25 million pounds of ground beef in 1997. E-mail to a friend .

The recall encompasses various brand names of ground beef patties produced by the Elizabeth, New Jersey-based company. In an official statement, Topps reported that the products may be contaminated with *E. coli* O157:H7, a bacterium capable of causing severe abdominal cramps, diarrhea, and other health complications. 

According to the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), 25 cases of illness are currently under investigation across eight states: Connecticut, Florida, Indiana, Maine, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, and Pennsylvania.

Additionally, we have augmented our internal quality control procedures with microbiologists and food safety experts. **WASHINGTON (CNN)** -- In one of the largest meat recalls in U.S. history, New Jersey-based Topps Meat Co. announced Saturday it is dramatically expanding a recall of frozen ground beef products to 21.7 million pounds due to potential *E. coli* contamination. 

The announcement vastly expands an initial recall issued on Tuesday, which originally covered 332,000 pounds of beef. 

Federal health officials said the tainted meat has been linked to at least 25 illnesses across eight states, mostly in the Northeast and Midwest. At least eight people have been hospitalized, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) issued a Class I recall, its highest threat level, warning that the consumption of the product could cause serious, adverse health consequences or death.

The expanded recall includes all frozen ground beef products produced by the Elizabeth, New Jersey, processor with "sell by" or "best if used by" dates between September 25, 2007, and September 25, 2008. The recalled items carry the establishment number "EST. 9748" inside the USDA mark of inspection.

"We deeply regret that any product we manufactured may have been linked to illness," Anthony D’Urso, chief operating officer of Topps Meat Co., said in a statement released Saturday. "Because of our commitment to food safety, we are taking this extraordinary step."

The problem was first discovered after state health departments in New York and Pennsylvania reported a cluster of *E. coli* O157:H7 infections. Subsequent testing by the USDA confirmed a match between a patient's illness and a sample of Topps frozen hamburgers.

*E. coli* O157:H7 is a potentially deadly bacterium that can cause severe abdominal cramps, bloody diarrhea, and dehydration. Children, the elderly, and those with compromised immune systems are particularly vulnerable to developing Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS), a severe type of kidney failure.

Officials expressed concern that because the recalled products are frozen, consumers may still have the contaminated patties stored in their home freezers. 

The beef patties were distributed to retail grocery stores, restaurants, and institutional food services nationwide. Popular brands included in the recall feature Topps, Walmart, Pathmark, and several private-label retail brands.

Dr. Richard Raymond, the USDA's undersecretary for food safety, urged consumers to check their freezers immediately and discard any affected meat. 

"If you have any of these products in your freezer, do not eat them," Raymond said. "Return them to the place of purchase or throw them away."

The 21.7 million-pound recall represents a devastating blow to the 67-year-old Topps Meat Co., covering roughly an entire year's worth of the company's production. 

Health officials remind the public that ground beef should always be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 160 degrees Fahrenheit to kill harmful bacteria, and consumers should use a meat thermometer to ensure safety.

*CNN's Medical Unit contributed to this report.*

# TOPPS MEAT CO. EXPANDS RECALL TO 21.7 MILLION POUNDS OF GROUND BEEF AMID *E. COLI* OUTBREAK

**ELIZABETH, N.J.** — In one of the largest food safety actions in U.S. history, Topps Meat Company has dramatically expanded its product recall to encompass an estimated 21.7 million pounds of frozen ground beef patties that may be contaminated with a dangerous strain of *E. coli* bacteria. 

The recall, announced in coordination with the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS), represents a full year's worth of production from the company's Elizabeth, New Jersey processing facility. 

The expansion comes just days after Topps initially recalled 332,000 pounds of frozen patties. Federal health officials upgraded the scope of the recall after state health departments linked Topps products to a growing outbreak of *E. coli* O157:H7, a potentially fatal strain of bacteria that causes severe abdominal cramps, bloody diarrhea, and in severe cases, kidney failure (Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome).

According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), at least 29 people across eight states—including New York, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Connecticut—have fallen ill in connection with the contaminated meat. Several individuals have required hospitalization.

### Company Leadership Responds

Executives at the 140-year-old company expressed regret over the outbreak and stated they are taking drastic measures to clean up their operations. 

"We are deeply grieved that any product we produced could be associated with an illness," said Anthony D’Urso, Chief Operating Officer of Topps Meat Company, in a statement released to the press. "Food safety has always been our highest priority, and we are working around the clock alongside federal authorities to identify the root cause of this contamination."

Geoffrey Levitt, Vice President of Operations at Topps, reiterated the company's commitment to consumer safety during a press briefing. "We are voluntarily taking this unprecedented step of expanding the recall because our primary concern is the health and well-being of our customers," Levitt stated. "We will not restart operations until we are 100 percent confident that our plant meets the highest standard of safety."

The USDA has suspended Topps’ operations at the Elizabeth plant after finding inadequate preventative measures against *E. coli* contamination, effectively halting all production.

### Affected Products

The recall covers all frozen ground beef products manufactured at the Elizabeth plant between **September 25, 2006, and September 25, 2007**. 

The products were distributed nationwide to supermarkets, retail grocery chains, and food service venues. Affected brand names include:
* **Topps**
* **Walmart** (select store-brand frozen patties)
* **Pathmark**
* **Fine Fare**
* **Super Fresh**
* **Ranchers Reserve**

Consumers can identify recalled products by looking for the USDA mark of inspection on the box. Affected products carry the establishment number **"EST. 974"** inside the USDA mark, usually accompanied by a "Best If Used By" date ranging between September 25, 2007, and September 25, 2008.

### How Consumers Can Get a Refund

Health officials are advising consumers to immediately check their home freezers, as frozen beef patties can remain stored for months without obvious signs of spoilage. 

**Do not consume the meat.** If you have any recalled Topps ground beef products, follow these steps to secure a refund:

1. **Return to Store:** Consumers can return unopened packages, opened boxes, or unused portions of the affected meat directly to the grocery store or retail outlet where it was purchased. Retailers have been instructed to provide a **full refund** upon return.
2. **Contact Topps Consumer Hotline:** Consumers with questions regarding the recall or refund procedures can call the dedicated Topps Meat Company Consumer Toll-Free Line at **1-888-734-0451**. 
3. **Safe Disposal:** If returning the product to the store is not feasible, consumers are urged to wrap the product securely in plastic bags and throw it away in an outdoor trash receptacle to prevent pets or wildlife from consuming it.

The USDA reminds consumers that the best protection against foodborne pathogens is to cook all ground beef thoroughly to an internal temperature of at least **160°F (71°C)**, verified using a digital meat thermometer.

***

*(Historical Note: Following this massive recall and the resulting loss of business and consumer trust, Topps Meat Company officially went out of business in October 2007, just days after announcing the expanded recall.)*

**MASSIVE MEAT RECALL: TOPPS MEAT CO. EXPANDS PULL TO 21.7 MILLION POUNDS AMID DEADLY E. COLI OUTBREAK**

**WASHINGTON** — In one of the largest meat recalls in United States history, the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) announced a massive expansion of a recall involving frozen ground beef patties from Elizabeth, New Jersey-based Topps Meat Company. 

The recall, which now encompasses an estimated 21.7 million pounds of ground beef products produced over a full year, was triggered by a growing multi-state outbreak of *Escherichia coli* O157:H7, a potentially deadly foodborne pathogen.

According to federal officials, the recall applies to all frozen un-cooked ground beef products manufactured at the facility between September 25, 2006, and September 25, 2007. All affected packages carry the USDA mark of inspection bearing **"EST. 9748"** inside the establishment number.

### A Rapidly Expanding Federal Investigation

The federal investigation began after state health departments and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) detected a cluster of severe illnesses across several eastern states, including New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Connecticut, and Florida. 

Initial epidemiological tracking by the USDA traced the source of the strain back to Topps Meat Co. On September 25, the company originally issued a localized recall of roughly 332,000 pounds of beef. However, as USDA inspectors deepened their investigation into the plant’s sanitation logs, safety procedures, and grinding records, federal officials determined that the risk of cross-contamination extended back a full year.

"FSIS safety officers determined that the company’s control measures were inadequate to ensure that *E. coli* O157:H7 was not introduced into the supply chain," said a USDA spokesperson during a press briefing. "Because the company integrated leftover production meat across multiple batch runs over several months without adequate intervention, we could not guarantee the safety of any product produced within that 365-day window."

At least 30 confirmed illnesses across eight states have been officially linked to the outbreak, with several individuals hospitalized due to Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS)—a dangerous type of kidney failure associated with severe *E. coli* infections.

### The Danger of *E. coli* O157:H7

*E. coli* O157:H7 is a bacterium that produces powerful Shiga toxins, which destroy red blood cells and damage the lining of the intestines and kidneys. Symptoms typically appear three to four days after exposure and include severe abdominal cramps, violent diarrhea (often bloody), and vomiting. 

While healthy adults usually recover within a week, young children, the elderly, and immunocompromised individuals face a severe risk of life-threatening complications. Ground beef is particularly vulnerable to *E. coli* contamination because the grinding process can distribute surface bacteria throughout the entire batch of meat.

### Historical Context: Standing Alongside Pilgrim's Pride

The staggering 21.7 million-pound size of the Topps recall places it among the most significant food safety disasters in American history. It ranks as the second-largest recall of ground beef in U.S. history, trailing only the 1997 Hudson Foods recall of 25 million pounds.

Industry analysts and public health experts are comparing the scale of the Topps crisis to the historic **Pilgrim's Pride recall of 2002**. In that event, poultry giant Pilgrim's Pride pulled a record-breaking 27.4 million pounds of ready-to-eat turkey and chicken products after a deadly *Listeria monocytogenes* outbreak caused 46 illnesses, eight deaths, and three stillbirths across the Northeast. 

While the Pilgrim's Pride recall remains the largest single meat recall by total weight in U.S. history, food safety advocates note that the Topps recall is uniquely alarming due to the length of time contaminated beef was distributed to retail stores, restaurants, and school lunch programs before federal regulators halted production.

"When you look at Pilgrim's Pride in 2002 or Topps Meat today, these mega-recalls expose systemic vulnerabilities in processing facilities," said food safety attorney Bill Marler. "A full year of production being called back indicates a total breakdown in safety protocols."

### Corporate Fallout and Consumer Guidance

The regulatory fallout for Topps Meat Company—a 67-year-old brand that was once the largest manufacturer of frozen hamburger patties in the United States—was immediate. FSIS formally suspended the assignment of federal inspectors to Establishment 9748, effectively forcing the facility to cease all operations. Facing massive financial liabilities, severe damage to its reputation, and a halt in production, company executives announced they are cooperating fully with federal regulators.

The USDA is urging consumers, food service operators, and retailers to check their freezers immediately for any frozen beef patties marked with **EST. 9748**. 

Because frozen ground beef has a long shelf life, officials fear that contaminated patties may still sit in consumers' home freezers. The USDA advises that any product matching the recall criteria should be wrapped securely and thrown away immediately or returned to the place of purchase.

Health officials also remind the public that ground beef should always be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 160°F (71°C), measured with a food thermometer, to ensure harmful bacteria like *E. coli* are completely destroyed.

```text
• Product: Frozen ground beef patties with sell-by dates between Sept. 25, 2007, and Sept. 25, 2008
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

*E. coli* O157:H7 is a potentially deadly bacterium that can cause bloody diarrhea, severe abdominal cramps, and in severe cases, Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS)—a type of kidney failure. Children, the elderly, and those with weakened immune systems are particularly vulnerable.

### **Advice to Consumers**

Federal officials are urging consumers to check their freezers immediately. The recalled products were distributed to retail grocery stores and food service institutions nationwide.

> **RELATED TOPICS**

> * [U.S. Department of Agriculture](javascript:void(0))

"Because these products are frozen, we are concerned that consumers may still have them in their home freezers," said Dr. Richard Raymond, USDA Under Secretary for Food Safety. "We urge everyone to check their freezers and throw these products away."

FSIS reminded consumers that ground beef should always be cooked to an internal temperature of 160 degrees Fahrenheit to ensure harmful bacteria are killed.

Topps, founded in 1940, had been one of the leading manufacturers of frozen hamburger patties in the United States.
